events.title: Basic Computer Course for Beginners / Computación Básica para Principiantes

cases.refreshed: Learn to use a computer with confidence! In this hands-on course, you'll learn the fundamentals of computers including how to use the keyboard and mouse, browse the Internet, use email, create documents, and more. Develop useful skills for school, work, and everyday life. Ideal for beginners. No prior experience required! Free. Bilingual. ¡Aprende a usar la computadora con confianza! En este curso práctico aprenderás los fundamentos de la computación, incluyendo el uso del teclado y el mouse, navegación por Internet, correo electrónico, creación de documentos y más. Desarrolle habilidades útiles para la escuela, el trabajo y la vida diaria. Ideal para principiantes. No necesitas experiencia previa. Gratis. Bilingüe

cases.refreshed: English Language Learners (ELL) can practice basic writing skills in English with our tutor in a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners. Sessions take place every 1st and 3rd (& 5th, if applicable) Tuesdays. Topics may include creating simple sentence structures, some basic grammar, and build up to writing a simple paragraph. Suggested for high beginners up to advanced English language learners. Space is limited and registration is required. Please stop by the Vineland Library or call us at (408) 808-3000 to register. Vineland's English Learning series: ELL Beginning English: A beginner program for learners with limited English skills; approximately levels 0-2; ELL Grammar and Vocabulary Club: An intermediate program for learners that know some English but want to learn more/complex English; approximately levels 2-3; ELL Conversation Club: An advanced program for learners to practice speaking and listening while also learning about American culture and idioms; approximately levels 3-4; ELL Writing Club: A program where high beginners to advanced level English language learners can learn and practice their English writing skills; approximately levels 2-4.

cases.refreshed: Are you a budding creative writer? Whether you've written for years or started yesterday, register for fresh inspiration to make your story shine! Young writers, 2nd Grade to 5th Grade (ages 7-11) are invited to join us for this creative writing workshop series hosted at the Pearl Avenue Branch Library. Attendees will learn to: Write fiction that reads like reality; Create characters that leave readers breathless; Identify plot points that serve multiple genres. This series will run from Tuesday, May 5th to Tuesday, December 15th, 2026. Please register for each session of this workshop you are looking to attend. Free. Registration is required. This program is generously sponsored by the Pearl Avenue Friends of the Library

events.title: Digital Skills: One-On-One Tech Help for Seniors

cases.refreshed: Do you have questions or need assistance with technology? At the Almaden Branch, you can make a 30-minute appointment for assistance with: Learning to use Libby (formerly Overdrive) to read ebooks and listen to e-audiobooks; Accessing non-Overdrive e-books and audiobooks from Boundless, Cloud Library, and Enki; Using Hoopla to read, listen and watch; Accessing the New York Times and/or the San Jose Mercury News online; Accessing and searching Consumer Reports; Learning a new language with Mango; Connecting to Wi-Fi/hotspots; Using Discover & Go to reserve free or reduced tickets to local museums and attractions; Navigating the SJPL website; Checking out a 7-day pass to access Great Courses from Libby or Hoopla; Using the library's pay-to-print system; Walking you through a Digital Skills Building Pathways lesson; And much more! By appointment only. One appointment per week per person. For questions, please call (408) 808-3040 or send an email to ab.sjpl@sjlibrary.org

cases.refreshed: Need homework help? Students in Kindergarten through 5th grade can meet with volunteer Homework Coach Delaney in the Children's Room to get homework support. Students must have assigned homework to work on to participate in a session. Homework Coaches can help look up and explain concepts covered on assigned homework, support students as they work through their assignments, check work, provide a set time to work on homework, and redirect focus as needed. Free, with limited capacity. The homework coach can work with up to 2 students at a time but can take new students if others finish their work early.

cases.refreshed: Come join teen-led group NeuroSphere! This session will dive into the basics of brain function, fun activities to test your brainpower, and an introduction to future career opportunities. There will be snacks; feel free to bring a friend! We're a group of high school students driven by a passion for neuroscience and the wonders of the brain. Our mission is to inspire curiosity and spark a love for science in younger students by creating engaging, hands-on learning experiences. Through NeuroSphere, we hope to share our knowledge, connect with the community, and encourage the next generation of future scientists and innovators! Questions? Email neurosphereyouth@gmail.com

cases.refreshed: Are you a second or third grader? Do you like to read books and talk about them with other kids? Then The Book Bugs Club is for you! Our November book selection is The Mystery of the Gold Coin by Harper Paris. At our book club meeting we will discuss the book and enjoy a fun craft or activity. Please pick up a copy of the book at the Children's Desk at Los Altos Library or at Woodland Library for check out. Please read the book at home before our meeting. Space is limited.
